asset-profile.formula: last close in the selected window against the window base; 10m/30m/1h use intraday bars, longer windows use daily
asset-profile.interpretation: One request covers the whole board, so the page is a single round trip. Outside the US cash session the Americas index rows swap to their CME futures proxy and are flagged as such.
asset-profile.limits: A CME proxy is a different instrument from the cash index and is labelled `is_cme_proxy`. Row status is one of intraday / delayed / end_of_day / unavailable and should be read before the number.
asset-profile.name: Board price and change

asset-profile.interpretation: Front-month futures, so a roll shows as a price jump that is not a market move.
asset-profile.limits: No term structure, roll yield or contango indication anywhere in the app; that would need a futures data vendor. Contract months are not labelled on the board.
asset-profile.name: Commodities

asset-profile.interpretation: Trades continuously, so these are the only rows that are live at the weekend.
asset-profile.limits: Spot only. No dominance, funding rate or open interest, which are perpetual-swap data and would need a derivatives source; Binance.US does not list perps.
asset-profile.name: Crypto

asset-profile.interpretation: Quoting convention differs by pair and is shown as labelled (EUR/USD versus USD/JPY), so the sign of a move means opposite things across rows.
asset-profile.limits: yfinance FX is indicative rather than a tradable quote and carries no spread. Weekend prints are stale from the Friday close.
asset-profile.name: FX pairs

asset-profile.interpretation: The board switches these rows to basis-point changes rather than percentage returns, because a yield going 4.00 to 4.66 has not returned 16%.
asset-profile.limits: The 2-year comes from FRED and updates on a different schedule from the yfinance rows beside it, so the curve can be internally inconsistent intraday.
asset-profile.name: US Treasury yields

asset-profile.interpretation: One batched request covers the whole board. Outside the US cash session the Americas rows swap to CME futures proxies and are flagged is_cme_proxy.
asset-profile.limits: A futures proxy is a different instrument from the cash index. Foreign indices show their last completed session, so a green row can be many hours old.
asset-profile.name: World equity indices

asset-profile.formula: std(daily returns, last 30) * sqrt(252) * 100; min(price/cummax(price) - 1) over 366 days
asset-profile.interpretation: The volatility figure is a 30-session window, so it reacts fast and will look extreme after a shock: the KOSPI reads 90% against a 52% one-year figure. The drawdown is the honest worst case an investor would have lived through.
asset-profile.limits: Realised, not implied, and backward-looking. The 30-day window and the 1-year drawdown are different horizons and should not be compared to each other.
asset-profile.name: 30-day volatility and deepest 1-year fall

asset-profile.formula: min/max of the last 366 calendar days of closes; position = (last-low)/(high-low)*100
asset-profile.interpretation: Position near 100% of the band means the asset is at its yearly high. Distance from high is the plain drawdown reading.
asset-profile.limits: Closing prices only, so it will differ from a vendor 52-week high computed on intraday extremes.
asset-profile.name: 52-week range and position

asset-profile.formula: counts of member day change sign; top-N cap sum / total cap
asset-profile.interpretation: Concentration is the number that explains why an index and its average member can disagree. The Dow shows 71.8% in its top 5.
asset-profile.limits: Day change is close-to-close from the batched download, so for a foreign index it is the last completed session, not live.
asset-profile.name: Constituent breadth and concentration

asset-profile.formula: last / close_at_or_before(today - window) - 1, per window; YTD uses 1 January
asset-profile.interpretation: Reading several windows together separates a trend from a bounce. Works for every row on the board, not just equities.
asset-profile.limits: Uses the last close at or before the anchor date, so a long market closure shifts the base. Price return only: no dividends, so equity index figures understate total return by roughly the yield.
asset-profile.name: Return ladder (1W-5Y)

asset-profile.formula: sequence of closes over the selected window
asset-profile.interpretation: Status is one of intraday, delayed, end_of_day or unavailable and should be read before the number itself.
asset-profile.limits: The sparkline is drawn from the same window as the selected performance period, so changing the window changes the shape as well as the number.
asset-profile.name: Row sparkline and status

asset-profile.formula: group members by sector; weight = sector cap / total cap; change = cap-weighted mean of member day changes
asset-profile.interpretation: Weighted by capital, not by headcount: the S&P has 75 Financials against 73 Information Technology names, but IT is 34.9% of the index and Financials 10.3%. Counting names would invert the picture.
asset-profile.limits: Each index publishes its own taxonomy and they are left alone: the Hang Seng ships 4 buckets, the FTSE 44. Not comparable across indices. 1,588 of 1,620 members carry a sector; the Straits Times table publishes none.
asset-profile.name: Sector mix

asset-profile.formula: last_level - level_at_or_before(anchor), rendered as basis points
asset-profile.interpretation: A 10-year going 4.00 to 4.66 has not returned 16%, it has risen 66 basis points. The panel switches to this reading automatically for the yield rows.
asset-profile.limits: Applies only to the yield section of the board. The frontend decides which reading to show from a `yields` flag, so a yield surfaced elsewhere would still print a percentage.
asset-profile.name: Yield change in basis points

asset-profile.formula: Scholes-Williams (1977): beta = cov(ln(1+r_asset), mr3) / cov(ln(1+r_mkt), mr3) where mr3 is the sum of the previous, current and next market log return. Correlation is taken at whichever of lag 0 or lag 1 reads stronger by at least 0.05.
asset-profile.interpretation: Beta near 1 means the asset moves with the S&P point for point. The Scholes-Williams form is used because most of the world does not trade while New York is open: Seoul closes at 06:00 UTC and New York at 21:00, so a same-day comparison put the KOSPI at beta 0.52 while it carried four times the S&P volatility. Corrected it reads 2.09. The panel says when a session offset was applied.
asset-profile.limits: The correction is near a no-op where sessions overlap, which is the check that it is not simply inflating everything: FTSE moves 0.31 to 0.36 while the KOSPI moves 0.52 to 2.09. Correlation cannot be summed the same way, so the lag is chosen from the data rather than a table of exchange hours. Needs 60 overlapping observations.
asset-profile.name: Beta and correlation vs S&P 500

asset-profile.formula: members from a bundled list; market cap = stored shares outstanding x live price x FX to USD
asset-profile.interpretation: Answers what an index is actually made of. Caps are computed live from a stored share count rather than a stored cap, because a cap is wrong by the next session while a share count moves a few times a year. Concentration (top 5 / top 10) is the fastest read on whether an index is really a basket.
asset-profile.limits: 1,620 of 1,741 scraped names resolved on Yahoo; the rest were dropped rather than shipped unpriced. Coverage is stated per index in the payload. London quotes in pence, so the FX conversion divides by 100 (case-sensitive on GBp vs GBP). The Dow and Nikkei are price-weighted, so a market-cap share column there is context, not influence, and the caption says so. Eight board indices have no free member list.
asset-profile.name: Index members with live caps

breadth.formula: count(close > rolling_mean(close, N)) / count(members with a defined N-session average), N in (50, 200)
breadth.interpretation: The participation reading. Above 50% is a broad market. The gap between the two lines is the cycle read: 50-day above 200-day is early recovery, 200-day above 50-day is late-cycle with short-term momentum fading. The S&P currently sits at 66% and 74%.
breadth.limits: Denominator counts only members with enough history, so a name added to the index last month is excluded rather than counted as "not above". Returns null, never zero, when no member qualifies. A 200-day average needs 200 sessions of run-up, which is why the download reaches back 520 calendar days.
breadth.name: % above 50-day / 200-day

breadth.formula: advancing / declining; null rather than infinity on a session where nothing fell
breadth.interpretation: Above 1 means more members rose than fell. Sustained readings above ~2 are broad buying; below ~0.5 is broad selling. It is a same-day snapshot, so read it with the A/D line rather than on its own.
breadth.limits: Undefined when no member declined. A single session is noisy; the A/D line is the version with memory.
breadth.name: A/D ratio

breadth.formula: cumsum(advancing - declining) over the last 126 sessions, rebased to 0
breadth.interpretation: The level means nothing; the shape against price is the whole signal. Index rising while the line falls means the rally is being carried by fewer names each week, which is the classic pre-correction pattern. The payload ships the index series alongside it so the two can be read on one chart.
breadth.limits: Rebased arbitrarily at the window start, so it cannot be compared across different window lengths or across indices.
breadth.name: Advance / decline line

breadth.formula: count(close_t > close_t-1) and count(close_t < close_t-1) across every member of the index
breadth.interpretation: The unweighted vote. 322 up against 177 means the average stock had a good day regardless of what the cap-weighted index printed. Compare it against the index move: a strong index day on weak advancers is being carried by a handful of large members.
breadth.limits: One vote per member, so a 0.01% move counts the same as a 9% one. Only the 17 indices with a tracked member list; the Russell 2000, Shanghai Composite, CSI 300, KOSPI, TAIEX, IPC and Bovespa have no free constituent list and return an explanatory message instead.
breadth.name: Advancing / declining

breadth.formula: sign(index change over 21 sessions) vs sign(A/D line change over the same window) -> narrowing | broadening | aligned
breadth.interpretation: Names the thing a breadth chart exists to show, so the reader does not have to eyeball two lines. Narrowing is an index rising on shrinking participation. Broadening is a decline the average member has stopped joining, which often marks the end of it.
breadth.limits: A plain comparison of two one-month changes, not a model and not a score. A 21-session window will call a mid-correction bounce "broadening". Both figures are printed next to the verdict so it can be checked.
breadth.name: Divergence state

breadth.formula: count(close >= rolling_max(close, 252)) and count(close <= rolling_min(close, 252)), min_periods 60
breadth.interpretation: An expansion in highs confirms a trend. An expansion in BOTH at once means the market is splitting rather than moving as one, which historically precedes trouble more reliably than either series alone.
breadth.limits: min_periods of 60 means a name with under a year of history can register an extreme against a partial window. Uses closes, not intraday highs and lows, so it undercounts against a vendor that uses the true range.
breadth.name: New 52-week highs / lows

chokepoint-exposure.formula: AIS position reports matched to a vessel registry and classified by type
chokepoint-exposure.interpretation: The live layer. Vessel type classification is what makes a tanker count meaningful rather than a boat count.
chokepoint-exposure.limits: Requires AISSTREAM_API_KEY, and the whole live maritime subsystem is gated off on Fly by ENABLE_LIVE_MARITIME, so production currently shows no vessels at all. AIS coverage is patchy beyond coastal receivers and transponders can be switched off.
chokepoint-exposure.name: Live vessel positions and classification

chokepoint-exposure.interpretation: The structural view of seaborne trade. The chokepoint history and comparison panels are built on the same feed.
chokepoint-exposure.limits: PortWatch lags 3 to 4 days, so it cannot show a disruption as it happens. That gap is the reason the live AIS nowcast exists alongside it.
chokepoint-exposure.name: Port calls and trade volumes

chokepoint-exposure.formula: PortWatch transit counts, with a status derived against the trailing baseline
chokepoint-exposure.interpretation: The structural series. A congested status against a multi-year baseline is more meaningful than a raw count, which is seasonal.
chokepoint-exposure.limits: PortWatch publishes 3-4 days behind, so this cannot show a disruption as it happens. Port ids are resolved by keyword at runtime, which is how the Danish straits map to Oresund.
chokepoint-exposure.name: Chokepoint transit counts and status

chokepoint-exposure.formula: curated company-to-chokepoint exposure map x a live disruption score per chokepoint, producing a signed score per ticker
chokepoint-exposure.interpretation: Connects a geopolitical event to a tradable list. Top beneficiary and most pressured are the two headline reads.
chokepoint-exposure.limits: The company-to-chokepoint mapping is curated by hand, not derived from disclosure, so it reflects a judgement about exposure rather than a measured one. A score of zero across all straits means no stress, not no exposure, and the panel says so.
chokepoint-exposure.name: Equity exposure to chokepoint stress

company.formula: -  (implied upside = target_mean / price - 1)
company.interpretation: The level of consensus. Implied upside against the current price is the headline, but the distribution matters more: a mean target hiding a 200-point spread is not consensus.
company.limits: Sell-side ratings skew structurally positive. Target dates are not published, so a stale target from a departed analyst can sit in the mean indefinitely.
company.name: Analyst ratings and price targets

company.formula: counts of strongBuy/buy/hold/sell/strongSell; mean recommendation score
company.interpretation: Read the distribution, not the mean. Sell-side ratings are compressed into the top half of the scale, so "hold" often functions as a sell.
company.limits: Coverage counts vary wildly by size; a mean over three analysts is not consensus.
company.name: Consensus recommendation and distribution

company.interpretation: The anchor every ratio on the page divides by, so a stale quote silently ages every multiple beside it.
company.limits: Delayed outside market hours. Extended-hours prints are shown where the source supplies them but are thin and can be crossed.
company.name: Current price and day change

company.formula: current assets / current liabilities
company.interpretation: The liquidity floor. Below 1 means the company cannot cover a year of obligations from current assets, which is normal for some models and fatal for others.
company.limits: A crude measure that treats inventory as liquid. The quick ratio, which does not, is not computed here.
company.name: Current ratio

company.formula: total debt / EBITDA
company.interpretation: Above 4x is where the credit panel colours red, and roughly where lenders begin imposing covenants.
company.limits: EBITDA is not cash flow. Meaningless for banks and insurers, which still render a value.
company.name: Debt / EBITDA

company.interpretation: A wall of maturities inside two years at rates above the existing coupon is a refinancing risk the leverage ratios alone will not show.
company.limits: Only issues captured in the filing extraction appear. Revolvers and undrawn facilities are usually absent, which understates flexibility.
company.name: Debt maturity ladder

company.formula: trailing 12m dividends / price * 100
company.interpretation: Rises mechanically when the price falls, so a high yield is as often a warning as an attraction. Check it against the payout trend rather than in isolation.
company.limits: Trailing, so a cut already announced but not yet effective still shows the old rate. Special dividends inflate it for a year.
company.name: Dividend yield

company.formula: sum of the last four reported quarterly diluted EPS
company.interpretation: The numerator behind P/E and the cleanest single profitability figure per share.
company.limits: Diluted or basic depends on what the source reported. Restatements are picked up silently on the next refresh.
company.name: EPS (TTM)

company.formula: gross profit / revenue
company.interpretation: Where pricing power shows first. A gross margin that erodes while revenue grows is the earliest sign of competitive pressure.
company.limits: Cost-of-revenue classification differs between filers and between SEC and vendor normalisations.
company.name: Gross margin

company.interpretation: Cluster buying by several insiders is the classic signal; a single sale is usually a scheduled 10b5-1 disposal and carries little information. Read the transaction classification, not just the direction.
company.limits: Form 4 has a two-business-day filing deadline, so the data is days old at best. Option exercises and tax withholding sales appear as transactions and dominate the raw counts. LSEG coverage is partial; most tickers fall through to yfinance.
company.name: Insider transactions (Form 4)

company.formula: -  (passive/active split comes from the LSEG rollup where it exists)
company.interpretation: High institutional ownership means the register is concentrated in hands that move in size. The passive/active split matters more than the headline: a name that is 40% index-held has a different float dynamic from one that is 40% actively held.
company.limits: From 13F filings, which cover long US equity positions only: no shorts, no derivatives, no non-US managers. Filed up to 45 days after quarter end, so it is up to four months stale at the end of a cycle.
company.name: Institutional and insider ownership

company.formula: EBIT / interest expense
company.interpretation: The input to the synthetic credit rating, and the threshold the panel colours red below 2x.
company.limits: Uses reported interest expense, which nets capitalised interest inconsistently. Undefined for a debt-free company, where it renders blank rather than infinite.
company.name: Interest coverage

company.interpretation: Context for a valuation gap: a name trading at a discount with recent approach activity is a different situation from one without.
company.limits: From a static bundled extract with no as-of date shown in the UI, so recent deals may be missing entirely.
company.name: M&A activity

company.formula: shares outstanding x price
company.interpretation: The size classification everything else keys off, and the denominator for the concentration figures in other tools.
company.limits: yfinance reports one share class, so a multi-class issuer (Alphabet, Berkshire, Ford) is understated against a full-float figure. Not adjusted for treasury stock.
company.name: Market cap

company.interpretation: The spread matters more than the mean. A tight cluster is real consensus; a 3x range between high and low means the sell side disagrees about the business, not about the price.
company.limits: No target dates are published, so a stale target from a departed analyst sits in the mean indefinitely. Structurally optimistic.
company.name: Mean, high and low price target

company.formula: total debt - cash and equivalents
company.interpretation: The figure that bridges enterprise value to equity value in every valuation model in the app.
company.limits: Period-end cash is seasonal for many businesses, so a single balance sheet date can misstate the steady-state position.
company.name: Net debt

company.formula: net income / revenue
company.interpretation: Read the gap against operating margin rather than the level. A widening gap is a financing or tax story.
company.limits: Contaminated by asset sales, impairments and tax one-offs that persist in TTM for a year.
company.name: Net margin

company.formula: operating income / revenue
company.interpretation: The operating leverage read: compare its trajectory against revenue growth to see whether scale is actually converting.
company.limits: One-off restructuring charges sit inside operating income for most filers and are not stripped out here.
company.name: Operating margin

company.formula: price / EPS (TTM)
company.interpretation: The most-quoted multiple and the least comparable across sectors. Only useful against the same company history or a genuine peer set.
company.limits: Meaningless on negative earnings and suppressed rather than shown negative. TTM includes one-offs, so a single impairment can distort it for four quarters.
company.name: P/E ratio

company.interpretation: The input to any sum-of-the-parts view, and the fastest way to see whether a "software company" is actually a hardware company.
company.limits: Segment definitions are the company own and change between years without restatement. The activity split (fees vs trading) only exists for financials.
company.name: Revenue by segment, geography and activity

company.formula: shares short; shares short / float; shares short / shares outstanding
company.interpretation: Percent of float is the meaningful version: 20% of a small float is a very different setup from 20% of outstanding on a mega cap.
company.limits: Float is sourced separately from the short figure and the two can be dated differently, so the ratio can be internally inconsistent by a couple of weeks.
company.name: Shares short and short % of float

company.interpretation: The raw position. On its own it says little: percentage of float and days to cover are the readings that matter.
company.limits: Biweekly and lagged: settlement is roughly two weeks behind and publication a week further, so this is never current.
company.name: Short interest

company.formula: mean daily volume over the trailing window
company.interpretation: The liquidity check that decides whether a position is exitable, and the denominator for days-to-cover.
company.limits: Shares, not dollars, so it is not comparable across price levels. A single block trade skews a short window.
company.name: Average daily volume

company.formula: cov(stock returns, market returns) / var(market returns)
company.interpretation: The textbook figure, shown so the divergence against the Scholes-Williams estimate beside it is visible rather than hidden.
company.limits: Biased toward 1 for thinly traded names because the stock return desynchronises from the same-day market move. That bias is exactly what the adjacent estimate corrects.
company.name: CAPM beta

company.formula: shares short / average daily volume, as published by FINRA
company.interpretation: Above 3 is the crowding threshold the panel colours amber at. This is the squeeze-risk number, because it measures the exit, not the position.
company.limits: Uses the volume regime at the settlement date. A subsequent volume surge makes the position far easier to cover than the published figure implies.
company.name: Days to cover

company.formula: consensus EPS now vs 7/30/60/90 days ago per fiscal period, as a percentage; up/down analyst counts over 7 and 30 days; price-target raises and cuts over 120 days
company.interpretation: Revision breadth is one of the more durable equity factors. NVDA currently reads rising: FY consensus +7.9% over 90 days, 4 analysts up and 0 down, 24 target raises and no cuts. A rising price on falling estimates is the configuration to be wary of.
company.limits: Counts are reported as counts and no score is derived from them, because four upgrades is four upgrades. yfinance reports a new coverage initiation with a prior target of 0, which is an absence rather than a target of zero and is nulled. Sparse or absent for small caps and most non-US listings.
company.name: Estimate revision momentum

company.formula: annualised standard deviation of the factor-regression residuals (IVOL); annualised stdev of raw returns (TVOL)
company.interpretation: High idiosyncratic volatility means the name moves on its own news, which is what a stock-picker wants and a diversifier does not.
company.limits: Residual to a specific factor set, so a missing factor shows up as idiosyncratic risk that is actually systematic.
company.name: Idiosyncratic and total volatility

company.formula: target_mean / price - 1
company.interpretation: Moves as much on price as on any change of view, so a rising implied upside during a selloff is usually the price falling, not analysts turning bullish.
company.limits: Inherits every bias in the target set. Not a forecast and not a probability.
company.name: Implied upside

company.formula: min(price/cummax(price) - 1); relative return vs benchmark over the window
company.interpretation: The pair answers "how much pain, for how much reward" in one line.
company.limits: Window-dependent and close-based, so intraday depth is understated.
company.name: Max drawdown and market performance

company.formula: per-holder pct_change since the prior filing; counts split at +/-0.5%; net = sum(shares * pct/(100+pct))
company.interpretation: The holders table is nearly static quarter to quarter; the change is the part that carries information and answers "what are funds accumulating". AAPL last filing: 5 added, 2 trimmed.
company.limits: yfinance reports a brand-new position as +100%, indistinguishable from a doubled one, so both are counted as "added" rather than guessed at. Same 45-day 13F lag as the ownership figures.
company.name: Quarter-over-quarter position changes

company.formula: cov(ln(1+r_i), mr3) / cov(ln(1+r_m), mr3) where mr3 sums the previous, current and next market log return
company.interpretation: The estimate to trust for an illiquid name. The app flags divergence from CAPM beta past 15% as a thin-trading warning.
company.limits: The 15% flag is a starting threshold, not a statistically derived cutoff, and the code says so. Daily frequency only; the lead-lag correction is meaningless at lower frequency.
company.name: Scholes-Williams beta

company.formula: interest coverage mapped to a rating through the Damodaran synthetic-rating table; Altman Z from the standard five-ratio formula; implied default spread from the same table
company.interpretation: A cheap sanity check on balance-sheet risk when no agency rating exists. Interest coverage under 2x and debt/EBITDA over 4x are the two thresholds the panel colours red at.
company.limits: Model-based, explicitly NOT an S&P/Moody's/Fitch rating, and the panel says so. Altman Z was fitted on manufacturers and is unreliable for financials, REITs and asset-light software. Falls back to a bundled Damodaran snapshot when live financials are missing.
company.name: Synthetic credit rating and Altman Z

correlation.interpretation: Turns a correlation matrix into something position-sizeable, since correlation alone says nothing about magnitude.
correlation.limits: Contemporaneous and uncorrected for session offsets, so foreign assets read low.
correlation.name: Beta to the benchmark

correlation.formula: Pearson correlation of daily returns over the chosen period
correlation.interpretation: The diversification check. Anything above roughly 0.8 is one position wearing two tickers.
correlation.limits: Cross-region pairs are understated by the same session-offset problem the Global Markets beta corrects for, and this tool does NOT apply that correction.
correlation.name: Correlation matrix

correlation.formula: correlation over a rolling N-day window
correlation.interpretation: The panel that matters: a static matrix hides that diversification disappears exactly when it is needed. Spikes toward +1 mark a risk-off regime.
correlation.limits: A rolling window trades responsiveness against stability; a short window produces swings that are estimation noise rather than regime change.
correlation.name: Rolling correlation

cot-positioning.interpretation: Extreme net positioning is a contrarian marker at the tails. Read the percentile against history rather than the raw contract count.
cot-positioning.limits: Published Friday for Tuesday, so it is always at least three days stale and often more. Covers futures positioning only: no term structure, no roll yield, and no commodity curve, which would need a futures vendor.
cot-positioning.name: CFTC commitments of traders

cot-positioning.formula: net = long contracts - short contracts per category; percentile against the trailing history of the same series
cot-positioning.interpretation: The percentile is the tradable version. A record net short by managed money is a contrarian marker; the raw contract count means nothing without that context.
cot-positioning.limits: Always at least three days stale and often more. Covers futures only, so a position hedged with options or swaps is invisible. Category definitions changed in 2009, which breaks long histories.
cot-positioning.name: Net positioning and percentile

credit-spreads.interpretation: The cleanest single read on financial stress. HY past roughly 6 points is genuine funding stress; CCC is the most recession-sensitive bucket and widens first.
credit-spreads.limits: Daily and index-level, so it lags an intraday risk event by a session. Option-adjusted, so it embeds a model of embedded optionality.
credit-spreads.name: IG and HY option-adjusted spreads

credit-stress.interpretation: The leading indicator of the three on this page. Standards tighten several quarters before delinquencies rise, so this is where a credit cycle turns first.
credit-stress.limits: A survey of senior loan officers, so it measures intent rather than realised lending. Quarterly and small-sample.
credit-stress.name: Bank lending standards

credit-stress.interpretation: The final confirmation, and the most lagging series here. By the time charge-offs rise the credit event has already happened.
credit-stress.limits: Lags delinquencies by roughly two quarters by construction, since a loan must be delinquent before it is charged off.
credit-stress.name: Charge-off rates

credit-stress.interpretation: The realised consumer stress read, and a lagging one. Credit card and auto delinquencies turn before mortgage.
credit-stress.limits: Lags the cycle by several quarters and is heavily revised. Aggregates hide the subprime cohort where the turn actually starts.
credit-stress.name: Delinquency rates

dcf-valuation.interpretation: SEC-first by design, so the statements come from the filing rather than a vendor normalisation wherever possible.
dcf-valuation.limits: Vendor fallbacks normalise line items differently, so a company switching source can shift a margin without the business changing. TTM figures lag the most recent quarter.
dcf-valuation.name: Financial statement inputs

dcf-valuation.formula: project revenue at a fading growth rate, apply an operating margin path, derive FCFF, discount each year at WACC, add TV = FCFF_final x (1+g) / (WACC - g), subtract net debt, divide by shares
dcf-valuation.interpretation: The output is a function of the assumptions, not of the company. Read the sensitivity grid before the point estimate: a 1pp change in WACC or terminal growth typically moves fair value more than any operating assumption.
dcf-valuation.limits: Terminal value is usually 60-80% of the total, so the perpetuity growth rate dominates. Requires WACC > terminal growth or the formula diverges. Beta and operating margin silently backstop from the bundled Damodaran snapshot when the vendor has no value, which is not a user-visible option.
dcf-valuation.name: Intrinsic value per share

dealer-gex.formula: argmax(net_gex) among positive strikes; argmin(net_gex) among negative strikes
dealer-gex.interpretation: Commonly read as magnet or resistance levels because dealer hedging concentrates there. Most useful near expiry, when gamma is largest and the effect is strongest.
dealer-gex.limits: A wall is only the biggest strike in the current chain; it moves when a single large position rolls. No implication that price will respect it.
dealer-gex.name: Call wall / put wall

dealer-gex.formula: sign x open_interest x 100 x charm x spot, per strike and expiry
dealer-gex.interpretation: Explains mechanical hedging flows into an expiry with no news, and is largest in the final days of a large open interest.
dealer-gex.limits: Same second-order estimation problem as vanna, and it grows without bound as time to expiry approaches zero, so the final session is unstable.
dealer-gex.name: Dealer charm exposure

dealer-gex.formula: sign x open_interest x 100 x delta x spot, aggregated per strike
dealer-gex.interpretation: Where dealers are long or short the underlying. Large negative delta above spot means hedging pressure builds as price rises into it.
dealer-gex.limits: Rests on the same sign convention as gamma: dealers assumed short calls and long puts. Frequently wrong for a single name with heavy retail call buying.
dealer-gex.name: Dealer delta exposure by strike

dealer-gex.formula: sign x open_interest x 100 x vanna x spot, per strike and expiry
dealer-gex.interpretation: The channel through which a volatility move forces spot hedging even when price has not moved. Matters most into a vol crush after an event.
dealer-gex.limits: Second-order greek computed from a chain IV that is itself derived from a mid price, so error compounds. Unreliable on illiquid strikes.
dealer-gex.name: Dealer vanna exposure

dealer-gex.formula: the same per-contract aggregation pivoted by expiration date
dealer-gex.interpretation: Shows how much of the exposure rolls off at the next expiry, which is the difference between a level that matters this week and one that matters all quarter.
dealer-gex.limits: Limited to 24 expiries. LEAPS carry small gamma but large delta, so a gamma-only read understates far-dated positioning.
dealer-gex.name: Exposure by expiry

dealer-gex.formula: walk strikes ordered by price, linear interpolation between the two strikes where net_gex changes sign, pick the crossing nearest spot
dealer-gex.interpretation: Above the flip, dealers dampen moves; below it they amplify. Traders treat it as a regime boundary rather than a target. Also available as an alert condition (price_cross_gex_flip) and stored in the GEX snapshot history so the level can be tracked over time.
dealer-gex.limits: Interpolated, not observed, so it is only as good as the strike spacing. On a thin chain the nearest crossing can jump several percent between sessions for reasons that have nothing to do with positioning.
dealer-gex.name: Gamma flip level

dealer-gex.formula: sign * open_interest * 100 * gamma * spot^2 * 0.01 / 1e6, summed calls positive and puts negative into net_gex per strike
dealer-gex.interpretation: Positive net gamma means dealers are long gamma and hedge against the move, damping volatility. Negative means they hedge with the move, amplifying it. The magnitude is dollars of hedging per 1% move, so it scales with the underlying and is not comparable across tickers of different price.
dealer-gex.limits: Assumes every open contract is dealer-short calls and dealer-long puts, which is the standard convention and frequently wrong for single names with heavy retail call buying. Open interest is previous-session settled, so intraday positioning is invisible.
dealer-gex.name: Net gamma exposure by strike

dealer-gex.formula: sum of net_gex across all strikes and expiries
dealer-gex.interpretation: The regime headline. Sign matters more than magnitude: positive damps volatility, negative amplifies it.
dealer-gex.limits: Not comparable across tickers, because it scales with spot squared and with open interest. A large number on a mega cap and a small one on a small cap can mean the same thing in relative terms.
dealer-gex.name: Total net gamma

debt-maturity.formula: -  (implied upside = target_mean / price - 1)
debt-maturity.interpretation: The level of consensus. Implied upside against the current price is the headline, but the distribution matters more: a mean target hiding a 200-point spread is not consensus.
debt-maturity.limits: Sell-side ratings skew structurally positive. Target dates are not published, so a stale target from a departed analyst can sit in the mean indefinitely.
debt-maturity.name: Analyst ratings and price targets

debt-maturity.formula: counts of strongBuy/buy/hold/sell/strongSell; mean recommendation score
debt-maturity.interpretation: Read the distribution, not the mean. Sell-side ratings are compressed into the top half of the scale, so "hold" often functions as a sell.
debt-maturity.limits: Coverage counts vary wildly by size; a mean over three analysts is not consensus.
debt-maturity.name: Consensus recommendation and distribution

debt-maturity.interpretation: The anchor every ratio on the page divides by, so a stale quote silently ages every multiple beside it.
debt-maturity.limits: Delayed outside market hours. Extended-hours prints are shown where the source supplies them but are thin and can be crossed.
debt-maturity.name: Current price and day change

debt-maturity.formula: current assets / current liabilities
debt-maturity.interpretation: The liquidity floor. Below 1 means the company cannot cover a year of obligations from current assets, which is normal for some models and fatal for others.
debt-maturity.limits: A crude measure that treats inventory as liquid. The quick ratio, which does not, is not computed here.
debt-maturity.name: Current ratio

debt-maturity.formula: total debt / EBITDA
debt-maturity.interpretation: Above 4x is where the credit panel colours red, and roughly where lenders begin imposing covenants.
debt-maturity.limits: EBITDA is not cash flow. Meaningless for banks and insurers, which still render a value.
debt-maturity.name: Debt / EBITDA

debt-maturity.interpretation: A wall of maturities inside two years at rates above the existing coupon is a refinancing risk the leverage ratios alone will not show.
debt-maturity.limits: Only issues captured in the filing extraction appear. Revolvers and undrawn facilities are usually absent, which understates flexibility.
debt-maturity.name: Debt maturity ladder

debt-maturity.formula: trailing 12m dividends / price * 100
debt-maturity.interpretation: Rises mechanically when the price falls, so a high yield is as often a warning as an attraction. Check it against the payout trend rather than in isolation.
debt-maturity.limits: Trailing, so a cut already announced but not yet effective still shows the old rate. Special dividends inflate it for a year.
debt-maturity.name: Dividend yield

debt-maturity.formula: sum of the last four reported quarterly diluted EPS
debt-maturity.interpretation: The numerator behind P/E and the cleanest single profitability figure per share.
debt-maturity.limits: Diluted or basic depends on what the source reported. Restatements are picked up silently on the next refresh.
debt-maturity.name: EPS (TTM)

debt-maturity.formula: gross profit / revenue
debt-maturity.interpretation: Where pricing power shows first. A gross margin that erodes while revenue grows is the earliest sign of competitive pressure.
debt-maturity.limits: Cost-of-revenue classification differs between filers and between SEC and vendor normalisations.
debt-maturity.name: Gross margin

debt-maturity.interpretation: Cluster buying by several insiders is the classic signal; a single sale is usually a scheduled 10b5-1 disposal and carries little information. Read the transaction classification, not just the direction.
debt-maturity.limits: Form 4 has a two-business-day filing deadline, so the data is days old at best. Option exercises and tax withholding sales appear as transactions and dominate the raw counts. LSEG coverage is partial; most tickers fall through to yfinance.
debt-maturity.name: Insider transactions (Form 4)

debt-maturity.formula: -  (passive/active split comes from the LSEG rollup where it exists)
debt-maturity.interpretation: High institutional ownership means the register is concentrated in hands that move in size. The passive/active split matters more than the headline: a name that is 40% index-held has a different float dynamic from one that is 40% actively held.
debt-maturity.limits: From 13F filings, which cover long US equity positions only: no shorts, no derivatives, no non-US managers. Filed up to 45 days after quarter end, so it is up to four months stale at the end of a cycle.
debt-maturity.name: Institutional and insider ownership

debt-maturity.formula: EBIT / interest expense
debt-maturity.interpretation: The input to the synthetic credit rating, and the threshold the panel colours red below 2x.
debt-maturity.limits: Uses reported interest expense, which nets capitalised interest inconsistently. Undefined for a debt-free company, where it renders blank rather than infinite.
debt-maturity.name: Interest coverage

debt-maturity.interpretation: Context for a valuation gap: a name trading at a discount with recent approach activity is a different situation from one without.
debt-maturity.limits: From a static bundled extract with no as-of date shown in the UI, so recent deals may be missing entirely.
debt-maturity.name: M&A activity

debt-maturity.formula: shares outstanding x price
debt-maturity.interpretation: The size classification everything else keys off, and the denominator for the concentration figures in other tools.
debt-maturity.limits: yfinance reports one share class, so a multi-class issuer (Alphabet, Berkshire, Ford) is understated against a full-float figure. Not adjusted for treasury stock.
debt-maturity.name: Market cap

debt-maturity.interpretation: The spread matters more than the mean. A tight cluster is real consensus; a 3x range between high and low means the sell side disagrees about the business, not about the price.
debt-maturity.limits: No target dates are published, so a stale target from a departed analyst sits in the mean indefinitely. Structurally optimistic.
debt-maturity.name: Mean, high and low price target

debt-maturity.formula: total debt - cash and equivalents
debt-maturity.interpretation: The figure that bridges enterprise value to equity value in every valuation model in the app.
debt-maturity.limits: Period-end cash is seasonal for many businesses, so a single balance sheet date can misstate the steady-state position.
debt-maturity.name: Net debt

debt-maturity.formula: net income / revenue
debt-maturity.interpretation: Read the gap against operating margin rather than the level. A widening gap is a financing or tax story.
debt-maturity.limits: Contaminated by asset sales, impairments and tax one-offs that persist in TTM for a year.
debt-maturity.name: Net margin

debt-maturity.formula: operating income / revenue
debt-maturity.interpretation: The operating leverage read: compare its trajectory against revenue growth to see whether scale is actually converting.
debt-maturity.limits: One-off restructuring charges sit inside operating income for most filers and are not stripped out here.
debt-maturity.name: Operating margin

debt-maturity.formula: price / EPS (TTM)
debt-maturity.interpretation: The most-quoted multiple and the least comparable across sectors. Only useful against the same company history or a genuine peer set.
debt-maturity.limits: Meaningless on negative earnings and suppressed rather than shown negative. TTM includes one-offs, so a single impairment can distort it for four quarters.
debt-maturity.name: P/E ratio

debt-maturity.interpretation: The input to any sum-of-the-parts view, and the fastest way to see whether a "software company" is actually a hardware company.
debt-maturity.limits: Segment definitions are the company own and change between years without restatement. The activity split (fees vs trading) only exists for financials.
debt-maturity.name: Revenue by segment, geography and activity

debt-maturity.formula: shares short; shares short / float; shares short / shares outstanding
debt-maturity.interpretation: Percent of float is the meaningful version: 20% of a small float is a very different setup from 20% of outstanding on a mega cap.
debt-maturity.limits: Float is sourced separately from the short figure and the two can be dated differently, so the ratio can be internally inconsistent by a couple of weeks.
debt-maturity.name: Shares short and short % of float

debt-maturity.interpretation: The raw position. On its own it says little: percentage of float and days to cover are the readings that matter.
debt-maturity.limits: Biweekly and lagged: settlement is roughly two weeks behind and publication a week further, so this is never current.
debt-maturity.name: Short interest

debt-maturity.formula: mean daily volume over the trailing window
debt-maturity.interpretation: The liquidity check that decides whether a position is exitable, and the denominator for days-to-cover.
debt-maturity.limits: Shares, not dollars, so it is not comparable across price levels. A single block trade skews a short window.
debt-maturity.name: Average daily volume

debt-maturity.formula: cov(stock returns, market returns) / var(market returns)
debt-maturity.interpretation: The textbook figure, shown so the divergence against the Scholes-Williams estimate beside it is visible rather than hidden.
debt-maturity.limits: Biased toward 1 for thinly traded names because the stock return desynchronises from the same-day market move. That bias is exactly what the adjacent estimate corrects.
debt-maturity.name: CAPM beta

debt-maturity.formula: shares short / average daily volume, as published by FINRA
debt-maturity.interpretation: Above 3 is the crowding threshold the panel colours amber at. This is the squeeze-risk number, because it measures the exit, not the position.
debt-maturity.limits: Uses the volume regime at the settlement date. A subsequent volume surge makes the position far easier to cover than the published figure implies.
debt-maturity.name: Days to cover

debt-maturity.formula: consensus EPS now vs 7/30/60/90 days ago per fiscal period, as a percentage; up/down analyst counts over 7 and 30 days; price-target raises and cuts over 120 days
debt-maturity.interpretation: Revision breadth is one of the more durable equity factors. NVDA currently reads rising: FY consensus +7.9% over 90 days, 4 analysts up and 0 down, 24 target raises and no cuts. A rising price on falling estimates is the configuration to be wary of.
debt-maturity.limits: Counts are reported as counts and no score is derived from them, because four upgrades is four upgrades. yfinance reports a new coverage initiation with a prior target of 0, which is an absence rather than a target of zero and is nulled. Sparse or absent for small caps and most non-US listings.
debt-maturity.name: Estimate revision momentum

debt-maturity.formula: annualised standard deviation of the factor-regression residuals (IVOL); annualised stdev of raw returns (TVOL)
debt-maturity.interpretation: High idiosyncratic volatility means the name moves on its own news, which is what a stock-picker wants and a diversifier does not.
debt-maturity.limits: Residual to a specific factor set, so a missing factor shows up as idiosyncratic risk that is actually systematic.
debt-maturity.name: Idiosyncratic and total volatility

debt-maturity.formula: target_mean / price - 1
debt-maturity.interpretation: Moves as much on price as on any change of view, so a rising implied upside during a selloff is usually the price falling, not analysts turning bullish.
debt-maturity.limits: Inherits every bias in the target set. Not a forecast and not a probability.
debt-maturity.name: Implied upside

debt-maturity.formula: min(price/cummax(price) - 1); relative return vs benchmark over the window
debt-maturity.interpretation: The pair answers "how much pain, for how much reward" in one line.
debt-maturity.limits: Window-dependent and close-based, so intraday depth is understated.
debt-maturity.name: Max drawdown and market performance

debt-maturity.formula: per-holder pct_change since the prior filing; counts split at +/-0.5%; net = sum(shares * pct/(100+pct))
debt-maturity.interpretation: The holders table is nearly static quarter to quarter; the change is the part that carries information and answers "what are funds accumulating". AAPL last filing: 5 added, 2 trimmed.
debt-maturity.limits: yfinance reports a brand-new position as +100%, indistinguishable from a doubled one, so both are counted as "added" rather than guessed at. Same 45-day 13F lag as the ownership figures.
debt-maturity.name: Quarter-over-quarter position changes

debt-maturity.formula: cov(ln(1+r_i), mr3) / cov(ln(1+r_m), mr3) where mr3 sums the previous, current and next market log return
debt-maturity.interpretation: The estimate to trust for an illiquid name. The app flags divergence from CAPM beta past 15% as a thin-trading warning.
debt-maturity.limits: The 15% flag is a starting threshold, not a statistically derived cutoff, and the code says so. Daily frequency only; the lead-lag correction is meaningless at lower frequency.
debt-maturity.name: Scholes-Williams beta

debt-maturity.formula: interest coverage mapped to a rating through the Damodaran synthetic-rating table; Altman Z from the standard five-ratio formula; implied default spread from the same table
debt-maturity.interpretation: A cheap sanity check on balance-sheet risk when no agency rating exists. Interest coverage under 2x and debt/EBITDA over 4x are the two thresholds the panel colours red at.
debt-maturity.limits: Model-based, explicitly NOT an S&P/Moody's/Fitch rating, and the panel says so. Altman Z was fitted on manufacturers and is unreliable for financials, REITs and asset-light software. Falls back to a bundled Damodaran snapshot when live financials are missing.
debt-maturity.name: Synthetic credit rating and Altman Z

dividends.interpretation: Turns a price-return book into something closer to total return. Ex-dates matter for anyone hedging around them.
dividends.limits: Historical dividends only; a forward estimate is an extrapolation of the last declared rate. Special dividends distort a trailing yield badly.
dividends.name: Dividends

dividends.formula: sum(shares * price) recomputed on each poll and appended to an in-session series
dividends.interpretation: Shows the day path rather than just the endpoint. The axis is deliberately a fixed numeric time axis with a stable value domain, because auto-scaling on a polling chart makes the line appear to jump on every tick.
dividends.limits: In-session only and not persisted, so a refresh restarts the curve. Built from polled marks, so a gap in polling appears as a straight line rather than as missing data.
dividends.name: Intraday book-value curve

dividends.formula: shares * live price; weight = position value / book value
dividends.interpretation: The live cockpit. Weight here is the input the Allocator rebalance reads as the current state.
dividends.limits: Options and futures are marked on a separate path and are excluded from the weighted equity legs handed to other tools, surfaced as a note rather than dropped silently.
dividends.name: Market value and weight per position

dividends.formula: shares * (price - avg cost); return = price / avg cost - 1
dividends.interpretation: Cost basis is user-entered, so this is only as accurate as what was typed. Imported books carry the basis from the import where the source had one.
dividends.limits: No lot-level tracking, so a position built in several tranches shows one blended basis and cannot produce tax-lot reporting.
dividends.name: Unrealized P&L and return

dividends.interpretation: The input every portfolio tool keys off. Books are importable into Allocator, Analysis, Compare, Backtester, Factor Decomposition and the drawdown alert through PMImportPicker.
dividends.limits: localStorage only, so it is per browser and never synced server-side. A drawdown alert therefore has to carry its holdings in the alert payload, the same way a strategy alert carries its rules. Clearing site data deletes the book.
dividends.name: Holdings, options, futures and cash

earnings.interpretation: Insider selling into a print is the context most often missing from an earnings preview.
earnings.limits: Same two-day filing lag and 10b5-1 noise as the Company Profile panel. Sparse for smaller names.
earnings.name: Insider transactions in the expanded row

earnings.interpretation: Context for the countdown without leaving the page. Falls back to the OHLCV route when the primary path returns nothing so the cell is never permanently blank.
earnings.limits: A short window, so it shows the run into the print rather than the trend. Not adjusted for the reaction gap being plotted alongside it.
earnings.name: Recent price series

earnings.interpretation: Two spines share one row type: a calendar window for the market and a countdown for names in your book, selectable per portfolio.
earnings.limits: The Finnhub free calendar is future-only and omits large caps such as NKE, which is why Nasdaq is merged in. yfinance drops the just-reported quarter for one to three days, which previously read in the UI as a date rescheduled months out.
earnings.name: Report date and session

earnings.formula: ATM straddle mid as a percentage of spot on the nearest expiry after the report
earnings.interpretation: Compare with the historical average absolute reaction below it: options consistently rich or cheap to realised is the tradable observation.
earnings.limits: Chain-derived from mid prices, so a wide spread inflates it. Needs a listed expiry close to the event; a name with sparse expiries gives a poor estimate.
earnings.name: Implied move into the print

earnings.formula: next-session close-to-close return following the report date
earnings.interpretation: The pairing with surprise is the whole point: a positive surprise with a negative reaction says the print was already in the price.
earnings.limits: A whole-session return attributes everything that day to the earnings print. For a before-the-bell report the reaction session is the same day, for after-the-bell it is the next.
earnings.name: Reaction: next-session move

earnings.formula: actual EPS - consensus EPS, and the same as a percentage of the estimate
earnings.interpretation: Only populates once a company has reported, so a blank means pending rather than missing. The percentage is the comparable version across price levels.
earnings.limits: Consensus is as captured near the print, not as it stood months earlier, so it understates how far estimates moved into the event. GAAP vs adjusted mismatches produce spurious large surprises.
earnings.name: Result: EPS vs estimate

earnings.formula: retrieval over the filing and release text, summarised by the LLM stack
earnings.interpretation: A reading aid over documents already fetched, generated on demand rather than for every row, with a visible progress percentage while it runs.
earnings.limits: Generated text: it can miss context and restate boilerplate as a finding. Never used to populate a numeric field on the page.
earnings.name: Quarter summary

factor-decomposition.formula: multivariate OLS of book returns on factor returns; risk shares from the variance contribution of each loading; annualised alpha from the intercept
factor-decomposition.interpretation: Tells you what a book is actually exposed to as opposed to what it holds. Risk shares sum to the systematic portion; the remainder is name-specific.
factor-decomposition.limits: Factor set is fixed at five and does not include size, value or momentum, so a style tilt shows up as unexplained alpha. OLS betas are unstable on under a year of data.
factor-decomposition.name: Factor exposures and alpha

fx-matrix.formula: cross rates derived from USD pairs; vol = stdev of weekly returns
fx-matrix.interpretation: The grid view for spotting which leg of a move is doing the work. The diagonal is blank by construction.
fx-matrix.limits: Crosses are derived from USD legs, so a synthetic cross carries both legs bid-ask, not the real quoted cross spread.
fx-matrix.name: Cross-rate matrix and volatility

global-markets.formula: last close in the selected window against the window base; 10m/30m/1h use intraday bars, longer windows use daily
global-markets.interpretation: One request covers the whole board, so the page is a single round trip. Outside the US cash session the Americas index rows swap to their CME futures proxy and are flagged as such.
global-markets.limits: A CME proxy is a different instrument from the cash index and is labelled `is_cme_proxy`. Row status is one of intraday / delayed / end_of_day / unavailable and should be read before the number.
global-markets.name: Board price and change

global-markets.interpretation: Front-month futures, so a roll shows as a price jump that is not a market move.
global-markets.limits: No term structure, roll yield or contango indication anywhere in the app; that would need a futures data vendor. Contract months are not labelled on the board.
global-markets.name: Commodities

global-markets.interpretation: Trades continuously, so these are the only rows that are live at the weekend.
global-markets.limits: Spot only. No dominance, funding rate or open interest, which are perpetual-swap data and would need a derivatives source; Binance.US does not list perps.
global-markets.name: Crypto

global-markets.interpretation: Quoting convention differs by pair and is shown as labelled (EUR/USD versus USD/JPY), so the sign of a move means opposite things across rows.
global-markets.limits: yfinance FX is indicative rather than a tradable quote and carries no spread. Weekend prints are stale from the Friday close.
global-markets.name: FX pairs

global-markets.interpretation: The board switches these rows to basis-point changes rather than percentage returns, because a yield going 4.00 to 4.66 has not returned 16%.
global-markets.limits: The 2-year comes from FRED and updates on a different schedule from the yfinance rows beside it, so the curve can be internally inconsistent intraday.
global-markets.name: US Treasury yields

global-markets.interpretation: One batched request covers the whole board. Outside the US cash session the Americas rows swap to CME futures proxies and are flagged is_cme_proxy.
global-markets.limits: A futures proxy is a different instrument from the cash index. Foreign indices show their last completed session, so a green row can be many hours old.
global-markets.name: World equity indices

global-markets.formula: std(daily returns, last 30) * sqrt(252) * 100; min(price/cummax(price) - 1) over 366 days
global-markets.interpretation: The volatility figure is a 30-session window, so it reacts fast and will look extreme after a shock: the KOSPI reads 90% against a 52% one-year figure. The drawdown is the honest worst case an investor would have lived through.
global-markets.limits: Realised, not implied, and backward-looking. The 30-day window and the 1-year drawdown are different horizons and should not be compared to each other.
global-markets.name: 30-day volatility and deepest 1-year fall

global-markets.formula: min/max of the last 366 calendar days of closes; position = (last-low)/(high-low)*100
global-markets.interpretation: Position near 100% of the band means the asset is at its yearly high. Distance from high is the plain drawdown reading.
global-markets.limits: Closing prices only, so it will differ from a vendor 52-week high computed on intraday extremes.
global-markets.name: 52-week range and position

global-markets.formula: counts of member day change sign; top-N cap sum / total cap
global-markets.interpretation: Concentration is the number that explains why an index and its average member can disagree. The Dow shows 71.8% in its top 5.
global-markets.limits: Day change is close-to-close from the batched download, so for a foreign index it is the last completed session, not live.
global-markets.name: Constituent breadth and concentration

global-markets.formula: last / close_at_or_before(today - window) - 1, per window; YTD uses 1 January
global-markets.interpretation: Reading several windows together separates a trend from a bounce. Works for every row on the board, not just equities.
global-markets.limits: Uses the last close at or before the anchor date, so a long market closure shifts the base. Price return only: no dividends, so equity index figures understate total return by roughly the yield.
global-markets.name: Return ladder (1W-5Y)

global-markets.formula: sequence of closes over the selected window
global-markets.interpretation: Status is one of intraday, delayed, end_of_day or unavailable and should be read before the number itself.
global-markets.limits: The sparkline is drawn from the same window as the selected performance period, so changing the window changes the shape as well as the number.
global-markets.name: Row sparkline and status

global-markets.formula: group members by sector; weight = sector cap / total cap; change = cap-weighted mean of member day changes
global-markets.interpretation: Weighted by capital, not by headcount: the S&P has 75 Financials against 73 Information Technology names, but IT is 34.9% of the index and Financials 10.3%. Counting names would invert the picture.
global-markets.limits: Each index publishes its own taxonomy and they are left alone: the Hang Seng ships 4 buckets, the FTSE 44. Not comparable across indices. 1,588 of 1,620 members carry a sector; the Straits Times table publishes none.
global-markets.name: Sector mix

global-markets.formula: last_level - level_at_or_before(anchor), rendered as basis points
global-markets.interpretation: A 10-year going 4.00 to 4.66 has not returned 16%, it has risen 66 basis points. The panel switches to this reading automatically for the yield rows.
global-markets.limits: Applies only to the yield section of the board. The frontend decides which reading to show from a `yields` flag, so a yield surfaced elsewhere would still print a percentage.
global-markets.name: Yield change in basis points

global-markets.formula: Scholes-Williams (1977): beta = cov(ln(1+r_asset), mr3) / cov(ln(1+r_mkt), mr3) where mr3 is the sum of the previous, current and next market log return. Correlation is taken at whichever of lag 0 or lag 1 reads stronger by at least 0.05.
global-markets.interpretation: Beta near 1 means the asset moves with the S&P point for point. The Scholes-Williams form is used because most of the world does not trade while New York is open: Seoul closes at 06:00 UTC and New York at 21:00, so a same-day comparison put the KOSPI at beta 0.52 while it carried four times the S&P volatility. Corrected it reads 2.09. The panel says when a session offset was applied.
global-markets.limits: The correction is near a no-op where sessions overlap, which is the check that it is not simply inflating everything: FTSE moves 0.31 to 0.36 while the KOSPI moves 0.52 to 2.09. Correlation cannot be summed the same way, so the lag is chosen from the data rather than a table of exchange hours. Needs 60 overlapping observations.
global-markets.name: Beta and correlation vs S&P 500

global-markets.formula: members from a bundled list; market cap = stored shares outstanding x live price x FX to USD
global-markets.interpretation: Answers what an index is actually made of. Caps are computed live from a stored share count rather than a stored cap, because a cap is wrong by the next session while a share count moves a few times a year. Concentration (top 5 / top 10) is the fastest read on whether an index is really a basket.
global-markets.limits: 1,620 of 1,741 scraped names resolved on Yahoo; the rest were dropped rather than shipped unpriced. Coverage is stated per index in the payload. London quotes in pence, so the FX conversion divides by 100 (case-sensitive on GBp vs GBP). The Dow and Nikkei are price-weighted, so a market-cap share column there is context, not influence, and the caption says so. Eight board indices have no free member list.
global-markets.name: Index members with live caps

housing.interpretation: The two inputs whose ratio drives affordability. Rate moves transmit to demand within a quarter; prices respond over years.
housing.limits: Some series in this tool run on a deterministic three-year mock cycle rather than live data, which is not distinguished in the UI.
housing.name: Home price index and mortgage rate

housing.interpretation: Permits lead starts, and starts lead completions by roughly a year, so permits are the forward-looking series of the three.
housing.limits: Extremely volatile month to month and revised heavily. Multi-family and single-family behave differently and are frequently reported together.
housing.name: Housing starts and permits

housing.interpretation: Six months is the conventional balance point. Below four is a seller market and is where price acceleration comes from.
housing.limits: National aggregates hide enormous regional dispersion, and no regional view exists in the UI despite a regional endpoint being available.
housing.name: Inventory and months of supply

implied-probability.formula: ATM straddle mid price as a percentage of spot
implied-probability.interpretation: The break-even move for an ATM straddle buyer, and the market consensus range into an event. Compare with the historical average move for the same event to see whether options are cheap or dear.
implied-probability.limits: A single-expiry snapshot from mid prices; a wide bid-ask on either leg inflates it. Says nothing about direction.
implied-probability.name: Implied move and straddle

implied-probability.formula: Black-Scholes risk-neutral probability from the chain implied vol surface, rendered as a density and a cumulative curve

insider-activity.formula: -  (implied upside = target_mean / price - 1)
insider-activity.interpretation: The level of consensus. Implied upside against the current price is the headline, but the distribution matters more: a mean target hiding a 200-point spread is not consensus.
insider-activity.limits: Sell-side ratings skew structurally positive. Target dates are not published, so a stale target from a departed analyst can sit in the mean indefinitely.
insider-activity.name: Analyst ratings and price targets

insider-activity.formula: counts of strongBuy/buy/hold/sell/strongSell; mean recommendation score
insider-activity.interpretation: Read the distribution, not the mean. Sell-side ratings are compressed into the top half of the scale, so "hold" often functions as a sell.
insider-activity.limits: Coverage counts vary wildly by size; a mean over three analysts is not consensus.
insider-activity.name: Consensus recommendation and distribution

insider-activity.interpretation: The anchor every ratio on the page divides by, so a stale quote silently ages every multiple beside it.
insider-activity.limits: Delayed outside market hours. Extended-hours prints are shown where the source supplies them but are thin and can be crossed.
insider-activity.name: Current price and day change

insider-activity.formula: current assets / current liabilities
insider-activity.interpretation: The liquidity floor. Below 1 means the company cannot cover a year of obligations from current assets, which is normal for some models and fatal for others.
insider-activity.limits: A crude measure that treats inventory as liquid. The quick ratio, which does not, is not computed here.
insider-activity.name: Current ratio

insider-activity.formula: total debt / EBITDA
insider-activity.interpretation: Above 4x is where the credit panel colours red, and roughly where lenders begin imposing covenants.
insider-activity.limits: EBITDA is not cash flow. Meaningless for banks and insurers, which still render a value.
insider-activity.name: Debt / EBITDA

insider-activity.interpretation: A wall of maturities inside two years at rates above the existing coupon is a refinancing risk the leverage ratios alone will not show.
insider-activity.limits: Only issues captured in the filing extraction appear. Revolvers and undrawn facilities are usually absent, which understates flexibility.

insider-activity.formula: trailing 12m dividends / price * 100
insider-activity.interpretation: Rises mechanically when the price falls, so a high yield is as often a warning as an attraction. Check it against the payout trend rather than in isolation.
insider-activity.limits: Trailing, so a cut already announced but not yet effective still shows the old rate. Special dividends inflate it for a year.
insider-activity.name: Dividend yield

insider-activity.formula: sum of the last four reported quarterly diluted EPS
insider-activity.interpretation: The numerator behind P/E and the cleanest single profitability figure per share.
insider-activity.limits: Diluted or basic depends on what the source reported. Restatements are picked up silently on the next refresh.
insider-activity.name: EPS (TTM)

insider-activity.formula: gross profit / revenue
insider-activity.interpretation: Where pricing power shows first. A gross margin that erodes while revenue grows is the earliest sign of competitive pressure.
insider-activity.limits: Cost-of-revenue classification differs between filers and between SEC and vendor normalisations.
insider-activity.name: Gross margin

insider-activity.interpretation: Cluster buying by several insiders is the classic signal; a single sale is usually a scheduled 10b5-1 disposal and carries little information. Read the transaction classification, not just the direction.
