insider-activity.name: Insider transactions (Form 4)

insider-activity.interpretation: Insider selling into a print is the context most often missing from an earnings preview.
insider-activity.limits: Same two-day filing lag and 10b5-1 noise as the Company Profile panel. Sparse for smaller names.
insider-activity.name: Insider transactions in the expanded row

insider-activity.formula: -  (passive/active split comes from the LSEG rollup where it exists)
insider-activity.interpretation: High institutional ownership means the register is concentrated in hands that move in size. The passive/active split matters more than the headline: a name that is 40% index-held has a different float dynamic from one that is 40% actively held.
insider-activity.limits: From 13F filings, which cover long US equity positions only: no shorts, no derivatives, no non-US managers. Filed up to 45 days after quarter end, so it is up to four months stale at the end of a cycle.
insider-activity.name: Institutional and insider ownership

insider-activity.formula: EBIT / interest expense
insider-activity.interpretation: The input to the synthetic credit rating, and the threshold the panel colours red below 2x.
insider-activity.limits: Uses reported interest expense, which nets capitalised interest inconsistently. Undefined for a debt-free company, where it renders blank rather than infinite.
insider-activity.name: Interest coverage

insider-activity.interpretation: Context for a valuation gap: a name trading at a discount with recent approach activity is a different situation from one without.
insider-activity.limits: From a static bundled extract with no as-of date shown in the UI, so recent deals may be missing entirely.
insider-activity.name: M&A activity

insider-activity.formula: shares outstanding x price
insider-activity.interpretation: The size classification everything else keys off, and the denominator for the concentration figures in other tools.
insider-activity.limits: yfinance reports one share class, so a multi-class issuer (Alphabet, Berkshire, Ford) is understated against a full-float figure. Not adjusted for treasury stock.
insider-activity.name: Market cap

insider-activity.interpretation: The spread matters more than the mean. A tight cluster is real consensus; a 3x range between high and low means the sell side disagrees about the business, not about the price.
insider-activity.limits: No target dates are published, so a stale target from a departed analyst sits in the mean indefinitely. Structurally optimistic.
insider-activity.name: Mean, high and low price target

insider-activity.formula: total debt - cash and equivalents
insider-activity.interpretation: The figure that bridges enterprise value to equity value in every valuation model in the app.
insider-activity.limits: Period-end cash is seasonal for many businesses, so a single balance sheet date can misstate the steady-state position.
insider-activity.name: Net debt

insider-activity.formula: net income / revenue
insider-activity.interpretation: Read the gap against operating margin rather than the level. A widening gap is a financing or tax story.
insider-activity.limits: Contaminated by asset sales, impairments and tax one-offs that persist in TTM for a year.
insider-activity.name: Net margin

insider-activity.formula: operating income / revenue
insider-activity.interpretation: The operating leverage read: compare its trajectory against revenue growth to see whether scale is actually converting.
insider-activity.limits: One-off restructuring charges sit inside operating income for most filers and are not stripped out here.
insider-activity.name: Operating margin

insider-activity.formula: price / EPS (TTM)
insider-activity.interpretation: The most-quoted multiple and the least comparable across sectors. Only useful against the same company history or a genuine peer set.
insider-activity.limits: Meaningless on negative earnings and suppressed rather than shown negative. TTM includes one-offs, so a single impairment can distort it for four quarters.
insider-activity.name: P/E ratio

insider-activity.interpretation: Context for the countdown without leaving the page. Falls back to the OHLCV route when the primary path returns nothing so the cell is never permanently blank.
insider-activity.limits: A short window, so it shows the run into the print rather than the trend. Not adjusted for the reaction gap being plotted alongside it.
insider-activity.name: Recent price series

insider-activity.interpretation: Two spines share one row type: a calendar window for the market and a countdown for names in your book, selectable per portfolio.
insider-activity.limits: The Finnhub free calendar is future-only and omits large caps such as NKE, which is why Nasdaq is merged in. yfinance drops the just-reported quarter for one to three days, which previously read in the UI as a date rescheduled months out.
insider-activity.name: Report date and session

insider-activity.interpretation: The input to any sum-of-the-parts view, and the fastest way to see whether a "software company" is actually a hardware company.
insider-activity.limits: Segment definitions are the company own and change between years without restatement. The activity split (fees vs trading) only exists for financials.
insider-activity.name: Revenue by segment, geography and activity

insider-activity.formula: shares short; shares short / float; shares short / shares outstanding
insider-activity.interpretation: Percent of float is the meaningful version: 20% of a small float is a very different setup from 20% of outstanding on a mega cap.
insider-activity.limits: Float is sourced separately from the short figure and the two can be dated differently, so the ratio can be internally inconsistent by a couple of weeks.
insider-activity.name: Shares short and short % of float

insider-activity.interpretation: The raw position. On its own it says little: percentage of float and days to cover are the readings that matter.
insider-activity.limits: Biweekly and lagged: settlement is roughly two weeks behind and publication a week further, so this is never current.
insider-activity.name: Short interest

insider-activity.formula: mean daily volume over the trailing window
insider-activity.interpretation: The liquidity check that decides whether a position is exitable, and the denominator for days-to-cover.
insider-activity.limits: Shares, not dollars, so it is not comparable across price levels. A single block trade skews a short window.
insider-activity.name: Average daily volume

insider-activity.formula: cov(stock returns, market returns) / var(market returns)
insider-activity.interpretation: The textbook figure, shown so the divergence against the Scholes-Williams estimate beside it is visible rather than hidden.
insider-activity.limits: Biased toward 1 for thinly traded names because the stock return desynchronises from the same-day market move. That bias is exactly what the adjacent estimate corrects.
insider-activity.name: CAPM beta

insider-activity.formula: shares short / average daily volume, as published by FINRA
insider-activity.interpretation: Above 3 is the crowding threshold the panel colours amber at. This is the squeeze-risk number, because it measures the exit, not the position.
insider-activity.limits: Uses the volume regime at the settlement date. A subsequent volume surge makes the position far easier to cover than the published figure implies.
insider-activity.name: Days to cover

insider-activity.formula: consensus EPS now vs 7/30/60/90 days ago per fiscal period, as a percentage; up/down analyst counts over 7 and 30 days; price-target raises and cuts over 120 days
insider-activity.interpretation: Revision breadth is one of the more durable equity factors. NVDA currently reads rising: FY consensus +7.9% over 90 days, 4 analysts up and 0 down, 24 target raises and no cuts. A rising price on falling estimates is the configuration to be wary of.
insider-activity.limits: Counts are reported as counts and no score is derived from them, because four upgrades is four upgrades. yfinance reports a new coverage initiation with a prior target of 0, which is an absence rather than a target of zero and is nulled. Sparse or absent for small caps and most non-US listings.
insider-activity.name: Estimate revision momentum

insider-activity.formula: annualised standard deviation of the factor-regression residuals (IVOL); annualised stdev of raw returns (TVOL)
insider-activity.interpretation: High idiosyncratic volatility means the name moves on its own news, which is what a stock-picker wants and a diversifier does not.
insider-activity.limits: Residual to a specific factor set, so a missing factor shows up as idiosyncratic risk that is actually systematic.
insider-activity.name: Idiosyncratic and total volatility

insider-activity.formula: ATM straddle mid as a percentage of spot on the nearest expiry after the report
insider-activity.interpretation: Compare with the historical average absolute reaction below it: options consistently rich or cheap to realised is the tradable observation.
insider-activity.limits: Chain-derived from mid prices, so a wide spread inflates it. Needs a listed expiry close to the event; a name with sparse expiries gives a poor estimate.
insider-activity.name: Implied move into the print

insider-activity.formula: target_mean / price - 1
insider-activity.interpretation: Moves as much on price as on any change of view, so a rising implied upside during a selloff is usually the price falling, not analysts turning bullish.
insider-activity.limits: Inherits every bias in the target set. Not a forecast and not a probability.
insider-activity.name: Implied upside

insider-activity.formula: min(price/cummax(price) - 1); relative return vs benchmark over the window
insider-activity.interpretation: The pair answers "how much pain, for how much reward" in one line.
insider-activity.limits: Window-dependent and close-based, so intraday depth is understated.
insider-activity.name: Max drawdown and market performance

insider-activity.formula: per-holder pct_change since the prior filing; counts split at +/-0.5%; net = sum(shares * pct/(100+pct))
insider-activity.interpretation: The holders table is nearly static quarter to quarter; the change is the part that carries information and answers "what are funds accumulating". AAPL last filing: 5 added, 2 trimmed.
insider-activity.limits: yfinance reports a brand-new position as +100%, indistinguishable from a doubled one, so both are counted as "added" rather than guessed at. Same 45-day 13F lag as the ownership figures.
insider-activity.name: Quarter-over-quarter position changes

insider-activity.formula: next-session close-to-close return following the report date
insider-activity.interpretation: The pairing with surprise is the whole point: a positive surprise with a negative reaction says the print was already in the price.
insider-activity.limits: A whole-session return attributes everything that day to the earnings print. For a before-the-bell report the reaction session is the same day, for after-the-bell it is the next.
insider-activity.name: Reaction: next-session move

insider-activity.formula: actual EPS - consensus EPS, and the same as a percentage of the estimate
insider-activity.interpretation: Only populates once a company has reported, so a blank means pending rather than missing. The percentage is the comparable version across price levels.
insider-activity.limits: Consensus is as captured near the print, not as it stood months earlier, so it understates how far estimates moved into the event. GAAP vs adjusted mismatches produce spurious large surprises.
insider-activity.name: Result: EPS vs estimate

insider-activity.formula: retrieval over the filing and release text, summarised by the LLM stack
insider-activity.interpretation: A reading aid over documents already fetched, generated on demand rather than for every row, with a visible progress percentage while it runs.
insider-activity.limits: Generated text: it can miss context and restate boilerplate as a finding. Never used to populate a numeric field on the page.
insider-activity.name: Quarter summary

insider-activity.formula: cov(ln(1+r_i), mr3) / cov(ln(1+r_m), mr3) where mr3 sums the previous, current and next market log return
insider-activity.interpretation: The estimate to trust for an illiquid name. The app flags divergence from CAPM beta past 15% as a thin-trading warning.
insider-activity.limits: The 15% flag is a starting threshold, not a statistically derived cutoff, and the code says so. Daily frequency only; the lead-lag correction is meaningless at lower frequency.
insider-activity.name: Scholes-Williams beta

insider-activity.formula: interest coverage mapped to a rating through the Damodaran synthetic-rating table; Altman Z from the standard five-ratio formula; implied default spread from the same table
insider-activity.interpretation: A cheap sanity check on balance-sheet risk when no agency rating exists. Interest coverage under 2x and debt/EBITDA over 4x are the two thresholds the panel colours red at.
insider-activity.limits: Model-based, explicitly NOT an S&P/Moody's/Fitch rating, and the panel says so. Altman Z was fitted on manufacturers and is unreliable for financials, REITs and asset-light software. Falls back to a bundled Damodaran snapshot when live financials are missing.
insider-activity.name: Synthetic credit rating and Altman Z
